## 債市主線

9月23日美國公債大幅下跌。美國企業活動轉強、能源壓力再起，加上$700億公債標售反應不佳，共同強化聯準會進一步緊縮的預期。10年期殖利率全日上升15個基點至5.11%；5年期券的市場殖利率則在標售後突破5%，為2007年以來首見。賣壓隨交易推進而加重：起初是對油價的反應，隨後擴大為對成長與通膨的重新評估，最後投資人更急切地要求提高承接新發公債的報酬。

9月企業調查初值顯示，製造業與服務業需求同步增強，供應延誤、聘僱與投入成本也加速上升。聯準會理事Michael Barr進一步表態支持調整政策。壓力並不限於公債，美國投資級債利差小幅擴大，高收益債利差明顯走闊，企業卻仍持續借款。軟銀完成大型美元及歐元債發行，美元部分的發行殖利率創自身紀錄，顯示市場仍有能力為大型投資計畫提供資金，只是代價已明顯提高。

## 需求轉強，公債標售承接疲弱

這波公債跌勢分階段加劇。油價先帶動歐洲與美國公債賣壓，美國活動數據接著增強進一步收緊貨幣政策的理由，5年期公債標售再令跌勢加速。彭博報導，10年期殖利率盤中一度上升近17個基點至5.13%，為2007年以來最高；5年期殖利率最多上升20個基點，債券價格寫下2024年以來最大跌幅，殖利率並突破2023年緊縮循環的4.99%高點。

標售得標殖利率為5.033%，相較發行前交易殖利率5.002%，尾差達3.1個基點。投標倍數為2.21倍，間接投標人取得54.3%、直接投標人29.9%，交易商承接15.8%。即使上午殖利率已大幅上升，投資人仍要求額外讓利。彭博指出，這次得標殖利率高於標售前市場水準的幅度，在其自2018年起的紀錄中排名第二，僅次於2022年6月；得標殖利率本身則是2006年以來最高。

整條殖利率曲線的變化顯示，除了通膨補償，實質借款成本也大幅調整。美國財政部每日固定到期殖利率參考值中，2年期上升14個基點至4.85%，30年期上升11個基點至5.40%。2年與10年期利差僅擴大1個基點至26個基點，2年與30年期利差反而收窄3個基點至55個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升13個基點至2.76%，同期損益兩平通膨率只增加2個基點至2.35%。因此，名目殖利率的漲幅主要來自實質殖利率，較符合市場預期政策將回應通膨的解讀，而非長期通膨補償出現同等幅度的上升。

標普全球9月綜合PMI產出指數初值由8月的56.0升至58.4，為2021年7月以來最高。製造業PMI由53.9升至57，高於市場預期的53.6；服務業由56.5升至58.7，也超過預期的56。需求並非集中在單一產業：綜合新訂單指數由55.2升至58.2，創2022年3月以來新高，兩大產業均有成長。

需求增強的同時，企業供給更為吃緊，成本也加速上升。未完成訂單升至2022年5月以來最高，供應商交貨延遲的普遍程度也為同年7月以來之最。投入價格指數由59.9跳升至66.4，為2022年10月以來最高；受訪企業主要歸因於燃料與運輸成本，許多企業也反映工資上升。整體就業增速為四年多來最快，其中製造業聘僱力道為2021年2月以來最強，新訂單成長則創2022年4月以來最快。

標普全球表示，調查結果對應約5%的GDP年化成長率；亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow估值為5.1%，相較之下，第二季實際成長率為1.5%。FHN Financial的Will Compernolle認為，經濟有韌性、足以承受緊縮，與經濟過強、持續製造價格壓力，是兩種不同情況，後者需要更急迫的政策回應。9月訂單增加、交貨時間拉長，正凸顯這個區別：需求持續成長，滿足需求的供給能力卻更吃緊。

Barr表示，通膨目標面臨的風險增加，勞動市場風險則下降，為及時恢復物價穩定，很可能需要進一步調整政策。路透將其發言解讀為暗示至少還要升息兩次，但Barr並未交代時間。他參與了前一週將聯邦基金利率區間上調至3.75%至4.00%的一致決議，這次談話則交代了他對兩項風險的最新評估。

市場也提高了升息預期。路透報導，週三上午短期利率期貨所反映的10月27日至28日會議升息機率，由當日稍早約55%升至近70%。到了稍晚交易時段，利率交換已完全反映未來一年升息三次、每次25個基點，並出現大量防範第四次升息的避險需求。

白宮國家經濟委員會主任Kevin Hassett週三在喬治城大學提出不同看法。他稱近期核心通膨的年化水準為2%，質疑升息必要性，並特別批評並非由總統川普任命的決策官員，也抨擊前主席Jerome Powell與前監理副主席Barr仍留任理事。這是政府對通膨與聯準會治理的批評；最近一次升息表決並未出現分歧，所有投票委員均投下贊成票，包括現任主席Kevin Warsh。

房市則呈現另一幅較弱的景象。美國抵押貸款銀行協會指出，截至9月18日當週，30年期固定房貸合約利率上升15個基點至7.12%，為2024年5月以來最高；五年期可調利率房貸卻下降13個基點至6.1%。房貸申請總量繼前週下滑4.1%後，再減少1.5%。購屋貸款申請下降0.8%，降至四週低點；轉貸申請減少2.6%，為2025年2月以來最低。

Nationwide經濟學家Ben Ayers認為，房市本身已陷入衰退，但其疲弱程度未必足以拖累整體經濟進入衰退。Nationwide預期房貸利率到年底仍在7%左右。Realtor.com的Hannah Jones則認為需求已接近底部，即使因機會而主動搬遷的家庭不多，人生階段的變化仍會支撐交易。企業調查雖然強勁，房市承受的融資壓力仍限制了整體成長的樂觀前景。

能源行情也扭轉了早盤對外交進展的樂觀。布蘭特原油在亞洲上午時段一度接近$98，彭博其後報導結算價上漲3.9%至$103.08。伊朗總統Masoud Pezeshkian週三在聯合國大會表示，只要制裁與美國封鎖持續，伊朗就不會允許荷姆茲海峽自由通行。他表達願意對話，但拒絕接受威脅，並捍衛伊朗使用民用核能技術的權利。這些條件使前一天較樂觀的談判消息，對近期局勢的意義受到限制。

實體原油定價另有壓力。WTI近月現貨相對次月交付的cash-roll溢價，自2017年有紀錄以來首次突破每桶$5。同時，白宮否認正準備實施90天柴油出口禁令的報導；能源部長Chris Wright表示，官員正與煉油商協調自願限制出口。干預措施的揣測帶動柴油期貨下跌，但煉油基礎設施受損、即期原油供應價格異常昂貴，仍使通膨前景更複雜。

美國財政部宣布，9月24日債券買回作業將接受最多$60億、剩餘期限20至30年的公債，為8月原先公布$20億的三倍。消息發布後，長債仍持續走弱。國際金融協會週三認為，次級市場買回可能帶來暫時紓解，卻無法修正債務攀升的結構性原因。這項措施為長端帶來潛在需求，但未能扭轉由最新總經資訊與標售承接疲弱所推動的跌勢。

iShares 20年以上美國公債ETF下跌1.6%，股價降至歷史新低$80.46。今年以來含配息總報酬為負4.8%，價格跌幅則為7.7%。其他市場方面，標普500下跌0.76%，美元指數上升0.68%至101.115，黃金期貨下跌1.16%。能源衝擊雖未化解，實質殖利率上升與美元轉強仍對黃金形成壓力。

## 通膨壓力延續，各國政策回應分歧

歐洲企業調查同樣加重公債壓力。歐元區綜合PMI由8月的52升至53.1，市場原本預期降至51.7，這次卻創三年多來最快擴張，服務業也意外改善。德國活動增速為2025年10月以來最高，法國則創兩年多來最快成長。

標普全球的Chris Williamson將德國帶動的製造業改善，部分歸因於AI與國防支出。製造業和服務業訂單同步增強，意味成長動能可能延續至第四季，但能源成本上升也加重通膨。彭博午後行情報導顯示，德國10年期殖利率上升9個基點至3.56%。歐元卻未受惠，在歐洲交易時段一度跌至$1.1409，為近兩個月低點，反映投資人更重視美國的成長與利率優勢。

投資人也透過選擇權布局歐元續跌。DTCC資料顯示，自聯準會會議以來，歐元兌美元選擇權名目金額約60%押注歐元走弱，相較之下，歐洲央行最近一次升息後，多空大致各半。看空歐元部位的加權平均到期時間也延長逾10%。德意志銀行的看法較不悲觀，認為全球成長韌性及美元自身風險可能限制歐元跌幅，儘管美國緊縮與能源成本會壓抑其上漲空間。

歐洲央行首席經濟學家Philip Lane週三表示，央行尚未看到能源衝擊引發顯著工資壓力，並提醒，不宜直接把市場定價全部解讀為預期升息。表面上，定價似乎顯示6月與9月升息後還有三至四次調整；但若剔除風險溢價，隱含利率高點只是明年略高於3%，並在2027年底前下降，相當於只反映再升息兩次。

Lane表示，能源價格到2027年中之前的走勢接近歐洲央行的不利情境，之後才回到基準路徑。天然氣儲存量約為70%，較歷史平均低16個百分點。德國最大工會正為約370萬名勞工爭取加薪5%，要求尚待協商，也使能源成本是否進一步推升工資與物價，仍是關注焦點。

經濟合作暨發展組織（OECD）最新期中展望，將通膨疑慮擴展至更廣泛的全球市場。受AI投資支撐，2026年全球成長預測由6月的2.8%上修至2.9%，2027年則由3.1%下修至3.0%。G20今年通膨預測由4.0%升至4.1%，明年由3.1%升至3.6%；除中國與沙烏地阿拉伯外，所有G20經濟體的2027年消費者物價預測均遭上修。

OECD預期聯準會今年再升息一次，歐元區、澳洲與南韓進一步溫和緊縮，日本也將繼續升息，英國與加拿大央行則暫時按兵不動。美國2026年與2027年成長率分別預估為2.2%及2.1%，通膨為3.6%及2.6%；歐元區兩年成長率均為1%。若能源壓力、強烈聖嬰現象、公債殖利率上升及AI報酬不如預期同時發生，其綜合不利情境將使2027年全球成長減少0.7個百分點、通膨增加1.1個百分點。

高盛週二發布、週三受到討論的研究報告，則預期緊縮不會如此持久。首席經濟學家Jan Hatzius認為，未來幾個月的消息將逐漸不再那麼偏向鷹派，部分依據是商品團隊預測布蘭特原油到12月將降至$85。高盛表示，中東出口已恢復至戰前近80%。其預測為聯準會10月完成最後一次升息、英國央行11月升息一次、歐洲央行12月完成最後一次調整，聯準會到2027年末才開始降息。這條比市場預期更短的緊縮路徑，關鍵在於能源成本回落的假設。

當前投資熱潮能否長期支撐成長，則是另一個問題。彭博經濟研究本週發布的預測認為，未來十年全球平均成長率為3.2%，低於疫情前的3.5%。人口結構、債務與全球化退潮料將拖慢成長，AI雖有望提升生產力，也可能擾動就業。

南非則已實際升息。貨幣政策委員會六名成員一致將基準利率上調25個基點至7.25%，有別於受訪經濟學家原先預期的分歧表決。總裁Lesetja Kganyago說，會中也討論過升息50個基點及維持不變；原先政策只有輕微限制性，持續性衝擊又可能影響通膨預期，因此決定加強緊縮。

南非8月通膨由4.3%升至4.4%，雖低於市場預期的4.5%，仍高於3%目標。南非儲備銀行將今年平均通膨預測由4%上修至4.4%，2027年由3.8%升至4%；2026年油價假設由$82提高至$90，2027年由$75升至$80。花旗的Gina Schoeman指出，一致表決及央行除燃料成本外也擔心服務業通膨黏著，都是重點。約翰尼斯堡午後交易時段，南非幣兌美元約貶值1.3%至16.39，10年期公債殖利率上升9個基點至8.90%。

英國面對的成長與財政組合較為不利。OECD預估今年與明年成長率分別為1.1%及1%，平均通膨為3.1%及2.6%，並呼籲加強支出節制與資源重新配置。週三公布的英國PMI相關報導顯示，融資與能源成本拖累活動，成長放緩。OECD認為英國央行可將利率維持在3.75%直到2027年中才開始降息，與市場擔心重新緊縮的看法不同。

英國首相Andy Burnham同時重申，英國對債券市場的依賴已過高，但強調他主張的是提高政府生產力、精簡政府運作。這番談話使政府在10月28日預算案前再受檢視。不過，彭博報導認為油價波動才是英國公債的主要影響因素，並指出自他上任以來，長天期殖利率大致未變。午後行情中，英國10年期公債殖利率上升11個基點至5.35%。

匈牙利則因政策可信度改善，債券受到投資人青睞。央行調降長期通膨目標後，10年期殖利率約為5.64%，低於波蘭的6.16%與羅馬尼亞的7.29%。德意志銀行估計，外資今年買進匈牙利本幣債約$135億，其中$100億是在4月大選後流入；債務管理局AKK資料顯示，8月底外資持有比重達34%，為2019年以來最高。

歐盟執委會週三因匈牙利新政府強化法治保障，建議釋出€42億的凝聚基金款項，進一步支持了投資人對匈牙利向歐洲其他市場靠攏的期待。不過，2026年財政赤字仍預估達GDP的7.5%，2027年預算與中期財政計畫因此攸關這波重估能否延續。

## 亞洲調整流動性與匯率防線

印尼央行連續第三次會議將政策利率維持在5.75%，符合36名受訪經濟學家中33人的預測，同時擴大吸引資本流入的誘因。這是Destry Damayanti正式就任總裁後的首次決策，措施包括將傳統證券投資避險換匯交易的加價最多調降25%，境內無本金交割遠期外匯的加價最多調降30%。優惠涵蓋證券投資、外國貸款與外人直接投資，資金承諾期間越長，折扣越大。

決策公布後，印尼盾保住稍早漲幅，兌美元升值0.4%至17,800，債券也維持上漲。Damayanti表示，經濟需要支持，而先前已預防性緊縮，目前政策利率仍足以維持穩定。8月通膨為3.2%，接近1.5%至3.5%目標區間上緣；銀行放款年增13.65%，超過全年預期的8%至12%區間。

央行持續在境內外干預，包括在次級市場買進公債。民間機構仍預期接下來可能升息：隆奧的Homin Lee認為，能源不確定性持續之下，央行12月將升息25個基點以支撐匯率；Bank Permata的Faisal Rachman也預期第四季升息，並指出若地緣政治緊張長期將油價維持在$100以上，進一步緊縮的機率會提高。

新加坡核心通膨連續第三個月加速，8月年增率2.2%，符合預期，為2024年9月以來最高；整體通膨2.3%，也與調查相符。食品、零售與服務價格漲勢加快，公用事業及其他燃料價格上漲6.1%。新加坡金融管理局與貿工部警告，外部投入成本將繼續沿供應鏈傳遞。核心通膨已接近金管局1.5%至2.5%預測區間上緣，預期要到2027年中左右才會明顯緩和。

中國人民銀行處理的則是更迫近的資金需求。人行宣布，黃金週前後可透過短期工具，每日提供最多人民幣1兆元、約$1,490億的流動性，9月28日至10月8日可進行隔夜逆回購操作。這段安排橫跨9月25日至27日及10月1日至7日銀行間債券市場休市期，為銀行提供假期與月底的流動性後盾。

中國利率相對平穩，也吸引了特殊的機構避險布局。法國巴黎資產管理的James McAlevey在本月稍早受訪、週三披露的訪談中表示，公司約自4月起買進墨西哥、巴西與哥倫比亞債券，同時透過放空離岸人民幣無本金交割利率交換避險，而非放空現券。他看好拉丁美洲市場的高實質殖利率與進一步降息空間，並認為若全球能源壓力與債市賣壓加劇，中國利率最終可能上升。

瀚亞投資的Rong Ren Goh描述了另一種跨市場調整：殖利率高於4%的30年期日本公債，若透過換匯轉為美元等已開發市場貨幣，避險後殖利率可能比相同基準貨幣的可比債券高100至200個基點。日本2年與30年期利差超過200個基點，其他核心已開發市場則約80個基點。瀚亞一方面增加較短天期美元債，一方面透過高品質公司債與武士債建立日本超長天期曝險。在市場預期日本政策利率最終由1.25%升至約2%的背景下，這項判斷著重匯率避險收益與曲線形狀。

菲律賓財政部長Frederick Go表示，零售公債即將發行，知情人士指出可能在10月推出，仍視市況而定。前次8月發行募得5,072億披索。零售債最低投資額為5,000披索，遠低於一般公債的1,000萬披索門檻，擴大了投資人參與範圍。

南韓國會議員另指出，德州一項金額達$223億的燃氣發電開發案，將是南韓對美投資安排下的首個項目，兩國總統也表示落實工作已有進展。

澳洲市場基礎設施仍受監管檢視。澳洲央行發現，澳洲證券交易所（ASX）一個或多個結算交割機構，在治理、全面風險管理、信用風險及作業風險方面僅部分符合標準。央行也肯定改善，包括將ASX Clear與ASX Settlement的作業風險評等由「未符合」提高為「部分符合」。不過，助理總裁Brad Jones表示，交易所在推動轉型計畫之際，重要領域仍未達標。

## AI發債完成定價，企業融資代價提高

軟銀完成約等值$110億的美元與歐元借款，將前期強勁認購意願轉為最終融資。美元部分包括$10億的3.5年期債、殖利率8.625%，$45億的5.5年期債、殖利率9.25%，以及$45億的7.5年期債、殖利率9.75%，均為其美元債歷來最高發行殖利率。€10億的歐元部分分為4年與6年期，其中6年期殖利率8%，也創軟銀同年期歐元債紀錄。

截至亞洲週三下午較晚時段，$100億美元部分的訂單已超過$300億，使最終殖利率得以下調至初步指引區間以下。彭博指出，完成這筆交易後，軟銀成為全球最大企業垃圾債借款人。認購需求依舊龐大，但基準利率上升與AI融資規模擴張，已提高公司履行投資承諾的資金成本。高盛信用策略師估計，2026年全球AI相關債務發行已超過$5,750億。

與CoreWeave相關的開發商Digital Drive也完成定價，以面額98.5%的價格發行五年期債券，募得$11億，殖利率9.25%，比同評等債券平均高約2.7個百分點。標普給予BB-評等，並將对單一投機級租戶的曝險列為主要風險。位於維吉尼亞州的規劃中園區，已全數由CoreWeave簽下15年合約，但預計2027年至2028年才開始營運。這次發行將先前推介的建設與租戶風險，具體反映在融資成本上。

AI借款也正在改變信用衍生工具市場。標普道瓊指數公司的Nicholas Godec援引DTCC資料指出，過去六個月Nvidia債務信用保護交易金額達$69億，前六個月僅$6.4億；交易激增是Nvidia納入週一生效之CDX投資級新系列的主要原因。隨借款與基礎設施承諾擴張，其違約保護成本今年已翻倍。

銀行也是信用保護的買方，藉此降低曝險，騰出空間與借款人承作更多業務。Godec表示，只要資料中心融資持續，AI相關交易增加的趨勢就看不到停止跡象。隨著初級市場發行擴張，大型科技企業的信用避險規模與流動性也在改變。

其他企業融資同樣活躍。AerCap Funding完成$15億優先無擔保債券定價，平均分為2030年到期、票息5.500%，以及2033年到期、票息5.875%的兩批債券。AerCap Holdings與部分子公司以優先無擔保方式提供完整且無條件保證。資金可用於飛機資產融資或再融資、償債及其他一般企業用途。

Bird.com取得$4億定期貸款與$5,000萬循環額度，由摩根大通主辦，Capital One及花旗參與。執行長Robert Vis表示，這筆融資將用於向股東與現任、前任員工分派股利，無須透過次級股權出售即可提供流動性。這家通訊服務公司去年EBITDA為$1.65億，約70%營收來自美國；這次借款是為了分配資金，而非新的收購或建設計畫。

Peloton在高盛安排投資人會議後，正考慮首次發行$8億債券，討論中的有擔保債殖利率約8%，尚未作出最終發行決定。這是整體借款利率；相較之下，其2024年槓桿貸款報價為浮動基準利率加約6個百分點，兩者計算基礎不同。

Ayala執行長Cezar Consing說明先前公布的三菱投資案資金用途時表示，這家菲律賓集團將取得約200億披索，用來降低負債、買回被低估的股票並支應成長。交易仍預期在三菱截至2027年3月的會計年度內完成。

併購活動持續帶來潛在融資需求。摩根大通全球併購主管Bouckaert週三表示，今年全球交易金額累計$2.5兆，動能很可能延續至2027年；總量較去年同期高約35%，科技交易接近增加60%。皇家加勒比另同意以約$30億收購Sandals Resorts半數股權。私人信貸方面則有不同訊號：投資人擔心貸款品質及傳統軟體業曝險，Apollo連續第三季限制一檔基金的贖回。

美國固定收益市場收盤後、紐約時間下午5時30分，加拿大皇家銀行宣布，透過加拿大中期票據計畫發行$15億具非存續觸發條款的或有資本（NVCC）次順位債券。票息在2031年10月1日前為4.67%，之後至2036年10月1日改為每日複利CORRA加1.16個百分點、按季付息。交易預計2026年10月1日交割；自2031年10月起可按面額贖回，但須事先取得加拿大金融機構監理總署（OSFI）批准，並提前30至60天通知。募集資金用於一般業務用途。

## 資本要求與債權回收前景改變

瑞士上議院就瑞銀海外子公司所需資本形式進行重要表決，結果未如瑞銀所願。議員以29票對16票支持，以股權資本覆蓋海外子公司價值最高90%，僅略低於政府原先100%的提案。瑞銀估計，國內法人將因此增加約$160億普通股權益第一類資本（CET1）需求；高盛與花旗分析師則估計接近$170億。

瑞銀原希望大幅提高可轉換額外第一類資本（AT1）債的使用，這次表決未採納其方向。額外發行AT1的可能性因而下降，帶動既有AT1價格一度上漲0.3美分至98.36美分。現行規定要求海外單位具備60%的資本覆蓋，其中四分之一可用AT1滿足；新提案將同時影響股權資本留存與未來次順位工具的供給。

瑞銀表示將繼續反對提案。財政部長Karin Keller-Sutter則認為，提高股權資本覆蓋可在危機時更容易處分海外業務，並保護瑞士母公司。法案接下來送交下議院，可能於今年底辯論，最終結果不太可能在2027年前出爐，也可能涉及公投。

泰晤士水務的優先債權人正準備作出更大讓步，以避免公司進入特別管理程序。成員包括Elliott、Silver Point與Farallon的London & Valley Water，正討論將債務減記幅度由原先30%提高至約35%。修訂方案可能包括約£35億股權資金，高於3月提案的£33.5億，另有£65.5億債務。金額仍在協商，最快10月可能提出新方案。

債權人也擬向專用營運改善基金投入逾£10億，較先前安排至少多£2億。泰晤士水務因漏水、污水排放等缺失，到本十年末可能面臨最高£8億的績效處罰，這些款項通常會用來減少用戶帳單。債權人希望改將隔離資金用於修復營運，理由是反覆處罰會壓縮處理缺失所需的現金；環境、飲用水及其他違法行為的法律罰款，則仍須另行支付。

擬議新股東承諾，在九年重整期間不領股利，成功後考慮重新上市。若公司改由政府控制，債權回收可能更低：Teneo去年分析估計，依營運表現而定，A類債權人每£1債權可能僅收回約50便士。目前民間方案仍在協商，政治反對已延後原先期待的監管協議與諮詢時程。

大宗商品貿易商Radiant World面臨的問題，則是帳上資產究竟有多少能用於償付債權人。提交法院的9月8日資產負債表顯示，總資產$10.72億中，貿易應收款占$10.07億，前十大應收款又占94%。彭博調查發現，其中相當部分來自否認欠款的交易對手、關係密切的貿易公司，或難以查找的實體。

最大列名欠款方Glencore International被列為積欠$1.504億，但嘉能可已提交通知，以Radiant欠其款項進行抵銷，並稱Radiant相關訴訟毫無依據。Vitol Asia被列為欠款$1.007億，維多則表示，早在數月前已停止與Radiant交易，所有交易均已結清。四家看似位於阿拉伯聯合大公國的公司合計占$3.29億，其中Milla Sky Trading占$7,600萬；其登記代表表示公司一年前已停止交易，並否認知悉Radiant或該筆債務。

對此，Radiant提供電子郵件截圖，內容看似由Milla Sky、Fly Horse及Bigbubble確認欠款。另有$6,480萬應收款列在Wuhan Iron & Steel Trading名下，但彭博無法辨識該實體；熟悉名稱相近之武漢鋼鐵母公司寶武的人士表示，寶武不承認這項債務。Radiant也為此提供電子郵件確認。另有$2.98億應收款來自關係密切的公司，包括Quanterra、Sapphire Minmetals與Grand Promise。

應收款爭議直接關係到公司控制權之爭。創辦人Pinkesh Nahar主張公司有償付能力，不需要司法管理人；瑞穗則指控詐欺，並質疑管理層誠信。應收款能否收回，是決定債權人可分配價值的核心問題；交易對手的否認與Radiant所提出的確認資料，仍都屬於有爭議的證據。

委內瑞拉債務處理在外交層面出現進展。美國國務卿Marco Rubio週三表示，川普與委內瑞拉臨時總統Delcy Rodriguez在週二聯合國招待會討論了主權債重整，財政部長Scott Bessent也在場。Rubio將經濟穩定與重建政黨、獨立媒體及可信選舉制度相連結。兩位總統直接交談，為約$600億違約主權債與委內瑞拉國家石油公司（PDVSA）債的談判，增添美國政治參與；若計入利息與仲裁求償，整體負債規模還要大得多。

歐盟官員另向烏克蘭表示，進一步戰爭援助需要相關立法取得進展，包括縮減地下經濟、強化稅收並使國內法規與歐盟法律接軌。這項條件意味烏克蘭的融資問題，不僅取決於外部支援，也涉及財政收入改革。

## 後續市場觀察

美國財政部週三宣布擴大買回規模後，長債價格仍未回穩，9月24日的實際作業將進一步顯示市場反應。重點是實際買回金額占$60億上限多少，以及成交價格。John Williams與Tom Barkin同日預定發言，全國企業調查明顯轉強，以及Barr對通膨風險增加、勞動市場風險下降的評估，將是這次政策討論的背景。

日本市場將於9月24日結束白銀週假期重新開市，迎接已改變的美國利率環境，以及連續四天貶值的日圓。日本央行近期升息後，海外債市賣壓將透過重新開市傳入國內交易。日圓走弱雖有助出口商，也可能加重輸入型通膨疑慮，干預匯市的預期則是另一項波動來源。

挪威與瑞典同日公布政策決定、新預測及利率路徑。週三隔夜利率交換顯示，挪威升息機率為60%，瑞典則為9%。若挪威升息25個基點至4.5%，瑞典維持1.75%，兩國政策利差將擴大至275個基點。挪威基礎通膨低於預期，使是否升息更難判斷；瑞典即使維持利率，國內動能增強與外部能源壓力也使前瞻指引格外重要。

週三美國收盤後，Bessent宣布，在與何立峰會面後，美中已同意將釜山協議延長至1月10日，解決了9月24日川習會前是否展延的近期疑問。Bessent說，官員正研究能否以一項更大的協議，取代接連簽訂的小型協議。因此，領袖會談的觀察重點轉為這項潛在安排的範圍；伊朗談判則仍面對Pezeshkian對制裁與封鎖提出的明確條件。

企業債務供給也有近期進度可看：花旗將在9月24日紐約時間上午10時30分展開Paramount貸款投資人會議，推進先前公布的收購融資分銷。此前完成的AI融資雖找到買方，卻須支付高殖利率。新加坡10月中旬政策決定將面對最新核心物價加速，泰晤士水務的修訂提案則將檢驗，更大債權人損失與更多營運資金，能否同時滿足監管機關與政府要求。

overall_summary.headline: 需求轉強、標售疲弱推升緊縮預期，美國公債大跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
9月23日美國公債大幅下跌，10年期殖利率全日上升15個基點至5.11%。賣壓最初來自能源，隨美國綜合PMI升至2021年7月以來最高的58.4，且投入成本漲勢加快、供應延誤拉長，市場轉而全面重估成長與通膨。聯準會理事Michael Barr表示，通膨風險增加、勞動市場風險下降，很可能需要進一步調整政策。

$700億的5年期公債標售再度加速跌勢，得標殖利率5.033%，尾差3.1個基點，並推動5年期券市場殖利率自2007年以來首次突破5%。10年期每日名目參考殖利率的升幅，主要來自實質殖利率上升，較符合市場預期政策將有所回應，而非長期通膨補償出現同等幅度增加。到了稍晚交易時段，利率交換已完全反映未來一年升息三次、每次25個基點。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off sharply on September 23 as stronger U.S. business activity, renewed energy pressure and a poorly received $70 billion auction reinforced expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. The 10-year yield rose 15 basis points to 5.11% over the session, while the auction pushed the traded 5-year yield above 5% for the first time since 2007. The decline gathered force as the day progressed: an initial response to oil became a broader reassessment of growth and inflation, then a more urgent adjustment to the price investors required to absorb new government debt.

September's flash business surveys showed demand strengthening across manufacturing and services while supply delays, hiring and input costs accelerated. Fed Governor Michael Barr added his support for further policy adjustment. The resulting pressure extended beyond government bonds: U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly and high-yield spreads widened noticeably. Nevertheless, companies continued to borrow. SoftBank completed its large dollar-and-euro offering at record yields for its dollar debt, illustrating a market still capable of financing ambitious projects, but at a substantially higher cost.

## Stronger Demand Meets a Weak Treasury Auction

The Treasury decline developed in successive stages. Oil-related selling first weighed on government bonds in Europe and the United States. The U.S. activity figures then strengthened the case for additional monetary restraint, before the 5-year auction accelerated the move. During trading, the 10-year yield rose almost 17 basis points to 5.13%, its highest since 2007, according to Bloomberg. The 5-year yield increased as much as 20 basis points, its largest selloff since 2024, surpassing the 4.99% peak reached during the 2023 tightening cycle.

The auction cleared at 5.033%, against a when-issued yield of 5.002%, producing a 3.1-basis-point tail. Bid-to-cover was 2.21; indirect bidders took 54.3%, direct bidders 29.9% and dealers 15.8%. Bloomberg described the yield concession against pre-auction trading as the second-largest in its records since 2018, exceeded only in June 2022. The auction yield itself was the highest since 2006. Investors required that additional concession even after the morning's substantial increase in yields.

The broader curve showed a large adjustment to real borrowing costs as well as inflation compensation. Treasury's daily constant-maturity references put the 2-year at 4.85%, up 14 basis points, and the 30-year at 5.40%, up 11. The 2s10s spread widened just 1 basis point to 26, while 2s30s narrowed 3 basis points to 55. At 10 years, the real yield increased 13 basis points to 2.76%, compared with a 2-basis-point rise in the breakeven to 2.35%. Most of the nominal increase therefore reflected higher real yields, consistent with an expected policy response to inflation rather than an equally large rise in long-term inflation compensation.

S&P Global's preliminary Composite PMI Output Index rose to 58.4 in September from 56.0 in August, its highest since July 2021. Manufacturing climbed to 57 from 53.9, against consensus of 53.6, while services advanced to 58.7 from 56.5, against expectations of 56. The strength was not confined to one industry: the composite new-orders index rose to 58.2 from 55.2, its highest since March 2022, with gains in both sectors.

The detail made the release more consequential than an isolated headline surprise. Backlogs reached their highest level since May 2022, and suppliers' delivery delays were the most widespread since July that year. The input-price index jumped to 66.4 from 59.9, its highest since October 2022. Respondents principally identified fuel and transport costs, but many also reported higher wages. Overall employment increased at its fastest pace in more than four years; within manufacturing, hiring was the strongest since February 2021 and new orders grew at their fastest rate since April 2022.

S&P Global said the survey was consistent with roughly 5% annualized GDP growth. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimate stood at 5.1%, compared with actual Q2 growth of 1.5%. FHN Financial's Will Compernolle distinguished between an economy resilient enough to withstand tightening and one generating additional price pressure through excessive strength. The latter, he argued, would require a more urgent response. September's combination of expanding order books and lengthening delivery times gave that distinction practical importance: demand was increasing while the capacity to meet it was becoming more strained.

Barr said risks to the inflation objective had increased while risks to the labor market had diminished, and that further policy adjustments were likely needed to restore price stability promptly. Reuters interpreted his remarks as suggesting at least two additional increases, although he did not specify their timing. Barr participated in the unanimous decision the previous week to raise the federal funds range to 3.75%-4.00%. His new comments supplied another policymaker's assessment of the balance of risks, rather than simply repeating that decision.

During Wednesday's morning trading, short-term rate futures put the probability of an increase at the October 27-28 meeting near 70%, up from roughly 55% earlier in the day, according to Reuters. By the later session, swaps fully reflected three quarter-point increases over the following year, with substantial hedging for a fourth. The changing near-term probability and demand for protection against an additional move captured the response to the day's stronger activity evidence.

National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett challenged the tightening case at Georgetown University on Wednesday. He characterized recent annualized core inflation as 2% and questioned the need for higher rates, singling out policymakers not appointed by President Donald Trump. He also criticized former Chair Jerome Powell and former supervision Vice Chair Barr for remaining on the board. Yet the latest increase had been supported by every voting member, including Chair Kevin Warsh. Hassett's argument represented the administration's assessment of inflation and Fed governance, not a split in the recorded policy vote.

Housing supplied a separate, weaker observation. The Mortgage Bankers Association reported that the 30-year fixed contract rate rose 15 basis points to 7.12% in the week ended September 18, the highest since May 2024. Total applications fell 1.5%, after a 4.1% decline; purchase applications dropped 0.8% to a four-week low, while refinancing fell 2.6% to its lowest level since February 2025. The five-year adjustable mortgage rate moved the other way, falling 13 basis points to 6.1%.

Nationwide economist Ben Ayers described housing as being in its own recession without necessarily being weak enough to pull the entire economy into one. Nationwide expected mortgage rates around 7% through year-end. Realtor.com's Hannah Jones thought demand was already near a floor, with life events sustaining transactions even when few households were moving opportunistically. Those assessments offered a concrete limit to the broader growth story: the strong business survey coexisted with a sector already bearing substantial financing restraint.

Energy trading also reversed the early optimism surrounding diplomacy. Brent traded near $98 in the Asian morning, but Bloomberg subsequently reported a 3.9% rise to a $103.08 settlement. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the UN General Assembly on Wednesday that Iran would not allow free passage through Hormuz while sanctions and the U.S. blockade remained. He expressed readiness for discussions but rejected threats and defended Iran's right to civilian nuclear technology. His position narrowed the immediate implications of the previous day's more encouraging account of talks.

Physical oil pricing showed another source of strain. The WTI cash-roll premium for prompt delivery over the following month exceeded $5 a barrel for the first time in records beginning in 2017. Meanwhile, the White House denied a report of preparations for a 90-day diesel-export ban. Energy Secretary Chris Wright instead said officials were working with refiners on voluntary export restraint. Diesel futures declined amid the intervention speculation, even as disrupted refinery infrastructure and exceptionally expensive immediate crude supply complicated the inflation outlook.

The Treasury also announced that its September 24 buyback would accept up to $6 billion of debt maturing in 20-30 years, triple the $2 billion originally communicated in August. Long bonds continued to weaken after the announcement. The Institute of International Finance argued Wednesday that secondary-market purchases could offer temporary relief without correcting the structural causes of rising debt. The announced operation added prospective demand at the long end, but did not arrest a selloff driven by fresh macroeconomic information and weak auction absorption.

The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF fell 1.6% to a record-low share price of $80.46. Its year-to-date total return, including distributions, was minus 4.8%, compared with a 7.7% price decline. Outside bonds, the S&P 500 lost 0.76%, the Dollar Index rose 0.68% to 101.115 and gold futures declined 1.16%. Higher real yields and the stronger dollar weighed on bullion even as the energy shock remained unresolved.

## Inflation Resilience Divides Global Policy Responses

Europe's own business surveys reinforced the pressure on government debt. The euro-area composite PMI increased to 53.1 from 52 in August, against expectations of a decline to 51.7, marking the strongest expansion in more than three years. Services improved unexpectedly. Germany recorded its fastest activity growth since October 2025, while France expanded at its quickest pace in more than two years.

S&P Global's Chris Williamson attributed the manufacturing improvement, led by Germany, partly to AI and defense spending. Stronger order books in both manufacturing and services suggested momentum could continue into Q4, while higher energy costs were adding to inflation. Germany's 10-year yield rose 9 basis points to 3.56% in Bloomberg's afternoon market account. The euro nevertheless weakened: during European trading it reached $1.1409, its lowest in nearly two months, as investors placed more weight on the U.S. growth and rate advantage.

The options response extended beyond immediate spot trading. DTCC figures showed about 60% of euro-dollar option notional positioned for euro weakness since the Fed meeting, compared with a nearly even split following the ECB's latest increase. The weighted-average expiry of bearish euro exposure lengthened by more than 10%. Deutsche Bank offered a less bearish assessment, arguing that resilient global growth and risks specific to the dollar could limit euro losses even as U.S. tightening and energy costs constrained its upside.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane supplied an important qualification to the inflation debate Wednesday: the bank was not seeing significant wage pressure in response to the energy shock. He also challenged a literal reading of market-implied tightening. Although pricing appeared to indicate another three or four moves after June and September, Lane said removing risk premia left an implied peak just above 3% next year, followed by lower rates by end-2027, consistent with only two further increases being priced.

Lane said energy prices were tracking the ECB's adverse scenario through mid-2027 before moving back toward its baseline. Gas storage was about 70%, or 16 percentage points below its historical average. A separate wage development showed why the second-round question remained active: Germany's largest labor union was seeking a 5% increase for about 3.7 million workers. That was a bargaining demand, rather than an agreed wage settlement, alongside Lane's assessment of the wage response already visible.

The OECD's new interim outlook broadened the inflation concern beyond individual markets. It raised its 2026 world-growth forecast to 2.9% from 2.8% in June, supported by AI investment, but reduced the 2027 projection to 3.0% from 3.1%. G20 inflation was forecast at 4.1% this year, up from 4.0%, and 3.6% next year, up from 3.1%. For 2027, consumer-price forecasts rose in every G20 economy except China and Saudi Arabia.

The organization expected one more Fed increase this year, further modest tightening in the euro area, Australia and South Korea, and additional increases in Japan. It expected the Bank of England and Bank of Canada to hold for now. U.S. growth was projected at 2.2% in 2026 and 2.1% in 2027, with inflation at 3.6% and 2.6%. Euro-area growth was forecast at 1% in both years. A combined adverse scenario involving energy stress, a strong El Nino, higher sovereign yields and disappointing AI returns would reduce 2027 world growth by 0.7 percentage point and raise inflation by 1.1 points.

Goldman Sachs presented a less persistent tightening outlook in a Tuesday research note discussed Wednesday. Chief economist Jan Hatzius expected the news to become less hawkish over coming months, partly on the commodity team's forecast that Brent would fall to $85 by December. Middle East exports had recovered to nearly 80% of prewar volumes, the bank said. Its forecasts envisaged a final Fed increase in October, a single BOE increase in November and a final ECB move in December, with Fed easing in late 2027. The assumed retreat in energy costs was central to that alternative to the market's more extended tightening path.

Longer-horizon research also pointed to a distinction between the current investment boom and trend growth. Bloomberg Economics' forecasts published this week put average world growth over the coming decade at 3.2%, compared with 3.5% before the pandemic. Demographics, debt and reduced globalization were expected to slow expansion, with AI capable of improving productivity but also disrupting employment. That projection concerned the next decade, not a revision to September's strong activity readings.

South Africa delivered an actual policy increase. All six members of the monetary policy committee voted to raise the benchmark 25 basis points to 7.25%, whereas surveyed economists had expected a divided vote. Governor Lesetja Kganyago said officials had discussed both a 50-basis-point increase and no change. Policy had been only marginally restrictive beforehand, he said, and the committee chose to add restraint as persistent shocks threatened to affect inflation expectations.

August inflation rose to 4.4% from 4.3%, below the 4.5% survey expectation but still above the 3% target. The SARB raised its average inflation forecast to 4.4% this year from 4%, and to 4% in 2027 from 3.8%. Its oil assumptions increased to $90 from $82 for 2026 and to $80 from $75 for 2027. Citigroup's Gina Schoeman highlighted the unanimous vote and concern about sticky services inflation alongside fuel costs. The rand was down about 1.3% at 16.39 per dollar in afternoon Johannesburg trading, and the 10-year government yield rose 9 basis points to 8.90%.

Britain faced a less favorable growth-and-fiscal combination. The OECD projected growth of 1.1% this year and 1% next year, with inflation averaging 3.1% and 2.6%, and called for stronger spending restraint and reallocation. Wednesday's UK PMI reporting indicated slower growth as financing and energy costs weighed on activity. The OECD judged that the BOE could hold at 3.75% until mid-2027 before cutting, contrasting with market concern about renewed tightening.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham meanwhile reaffirmed his view that Britain had become excessively exposed to bond markets, while saying his argument was for a more productive, streamlined state. The comments revived scrutiny ahead of the October 28 budget, but Bloomberg's account identified oil swings as the dominant influence on gilts and noted that long yields were broadly unchanged since he became premier. The 10-year gilt yield rose 11 basis points to 5.35% in the afternoon market account.

Hungarian debt drew a different response to policy credibility. After the central bank's reduction of its long-run inflation target, the 10-year yield was about 5.64%, below Poland's 6.16% and Romania's 7.29%. Deutsche Bank estimated foreign purchases of Hungarian local bonds at $13.5 billion this year, including $10 billion since April's election. Foreign ownership reached 34% at August's end, its highest since 2019, according to debt agency AKK.

The European Commission added a tangible development Wednesday by proposing to release EUR4.2 billion of cohesion funding after the new Hungarian government strengthened rule-of-law safeguards. That specific proposal accompanied the broader convergence enthusiasm. Investors still faced a projected 2026 deficit of 7.5% of GDP, leaving the 2027 budget and medium-term fiscal plan important to sustaining the repricing.

## Asian Authorities Adjust Liquidity and Currency Defenses

Bank Indonesia held its policy rate at 5.75% for a third meeting, matching 33 of 36 economist forecasts, while expanding incentives intended to attract capital. Governor Destry Damayanti's first decision since taking the permanent post reduced premiums for conventional portfolio-investment hedging swaps by up to 25% and domestic non-deliverable forwards by up to 30%. The incentives cover portfolio investment, foreign loans and foreign direct investment, with larger discounts for funds committed for longer periods.

The rupiah retained earlier gains after the announcement, strengthening 0.4% to 17,800 per dollar, while bonds also held their advance. Damayanti said the economy needed support and the current policy rate remained adequate for stability after earlier preemptive tightening. August inflation was 3.2%, near the top of the 1.5%-3.5% target band, while bank lending grew 13.65% from a year earlier, exceeding the year's 8%-12% expected range.

The central bank continued intervention offshore and onshore, including secondary-market government-bond purchases. Lombard Odier's Homin Lee still expected a quarter-point increase in December to support the currency as energy uncertainty persisted. Bank Permata's Faisal Rachman also expected a Q4 increase and said prolonged geopolitical tension keeping oil above $100 would increase the likelihood of more tightening. The decision therefore expanded the currency-defense tools in use without endorsing those private forecasts of the next rate move.

Singapore reported a third consecutive acceleration in core inflation. August's 2.2% annual rate matched expectations and was the highest since September 2024; headline inflation was 2.3%, also in line with the survey. Food, retail and services prices accelerated, while utilities and other fuels rose 6.1%. The Monetary Authority of Singapore and trade ministry warned that external input costs would continue passing through supply chains. Core inflation was approaching the upper end of the MAS's 1.5%-2.5% forecast range, with a discernible moderation expected only around mid-2027.

China's central bank addressed a nearer-term funding problem. The PBOC announced capacity to provide up to CNY1 trillion, about $149 billion, a day through short-term tools around Golden Week. Overnight reverse-repo operations will be available from September 28 through October 8. The window spans interbank bond-market closures on September 25-27 and October 1-7, giving banks a liquidity backstop across the holiday and month-end period.

The relative calm in Chinese rates has also attracted a distinctive institutional hedge. BNP Paribas Asset Management's James McAlevey said in an interview earlier this month that the manager had been buying debt in Mexico, Brazil and Colombia since around April while shorting offshore Chinese non-deliverable interest-rate swaps. He favored the Latin American markets' high real yields and potential for further easing, while expecting Chinese rates could eventually rise if global energy pressure and the bond selloff intensified. The positions use derivatives rather than short cash bonds; they were described Wednesday, not initiated as a response to that day's U.S. trading.

Eastspring's Rong Ren Goh described a different cross-market shift. A 30-year JGB yielding above 4%, swapped into a developed-market currency including dollars, could offer a hedged yield 100-200 basis points above a comparable base-currency bond, he said. Japan's 2s30s curve exceeded 200 basis points, against roughly 80 across other core developed markets. Eastspring was adding shorter-dated dollar debt while building ultra-long Japanese exposure through high-quality corporate and Samurai bonds. Its assessment focused on hedge economics and curve shape as markets anticipated an eventual Japanese policy rate around 2%, from 1.25%.

In the Philippines, Finance Secretary Frederick Go said a retail Treasury bond offering was approaching, with people familiar with the plans pointing to October subject to market conditions. The previous August sale raised PHP507.2 billion. Retail securities permit investments from PHP5,000, broadening access well beyond the PHP10 million minimum for conventional government debt. Separately, South Korean lawmakers identified a $22.3 billion Texas gas-fired power development as the first project under the country's U.S. investment arrangement, as the two presidents reported progress on implementation.

Australian market infrastructure remained under regulatory scrutiny. The RBA found that one or more ASX clearing and settlement facilities only partly met standards for governance, comprehensive risk management, credit risk and operational risk. It acknowledged improvements, including an upgrade of operational-risk assessments for ASX Clear and ASX Settlement from not observed to partly observed, but Assistant Governor Brad Jones said the exchange still fell short in important areas while carrying out its transformation program.

## Corporate Borrowers Pay Up as AI Deals Price

SoftBank completed approximately $11 billion equivalent of dollar and euro borrowing, converting strong preliminary interest into final financing terms. It sold $1 billion of 3.5-year dollar notes at 8.625%, $4.5 billion of 5.5-year notes at 9.25% and $4.5 billion of 7.5-year securities at 9.75%. These were record issuance yields for its dollar bonds. The EUR1 billion euro component was divided between four- and six-year maturities, with the longer tranche yielding 8%, a record for SoftBank at that tenor in euros.

Orders for the $10 billion dollar portion exceeded $30 billion by late Wednesday afternoon in Asia, allowing yields to fall from initial ranges. The completed transaction made SoftBank the world's largest corporate junk-bond borrower, according to Bloomberg. Demand remained substantial even as the rise in benchmark rates and the scale of AI financing raised the cost of funding the company's investment commitments. Goldman Sachs credit strategists put global AI-related debt issuance above $575 billion in 2026.

Digital Drive's CoreWeave-linked financing also reached final terms. The developer raised $1.1 billion through five-year notes priced at 98.5 cents to yield 9.25%, about 2.7 percentage points above the average for similarly rated debt. S&P assigned BB- and identified exposure to a single speculative-grade tenant as the main risk. The future Virginia campus is fully committed to CoreWeave under a 15-year contract, but operations are expected only in 2027-2028. The completed sale establishes the financing cost for that construction and tenant exposure after earlier marketing.

AI borrowing is also changing the credit-derivatives market. Protection traded on $6.9 billion of Nvidia debt over the past six months, compared with $640 million in the preceding six, S&P Dow Jones Indices' Nicholas Godec said, citing DTCC data. The surge was the principal reason for Nvidia's inclusion in the CDX Investment-Grade series that took effect Monday. Its default-protection cost had doubled this year as borrowing and infrastructure commitments expanded.

Banks are among the buyers of that protection, reducing exposure so they can conduct more business with the borrowers. Godec said the pickup in AI-related trading showed no sign of stopping as data-center financing continued. This is a change in the scale and liquidity of hedging around large technology credits, alongside primary issuance, rather than a single issuer's funding transaction alone.

The wider corporate market remained active. AerCap Funding priced $1.5 billion of senior unsecured notes, divided equally between 5.500% debt due in 2030 and 5.875% debt due in 2033. AerCap Holdings and certain subsidiaries fully and unconditionally guarantee the notes on a senior unsecured basis. Proceeds can finance or refinance aircraft assets, repay debt and support other corporate purposes.

Bird.com raised a $400 million term loan and $50 million revolving facility, led by JPMorgan with participation from Capital One and Citigroup. Chief Executive Robert Vis said the financing would support a dividend to shareholders and current and former employees, providing liquidity without a secondary share sale. The messaging company reported $165 million of EBITDA last year and derives about 70% of revenue from the United States. Its borrowing finances distributions rather than a new acquisition or construction project.

Peloton was considering an $800 million debut bond offering after investor meetings arranged by Goldman Sachs. Discussions concerned secured debt yielding about 8%, with no final issuance decision. Its 2024 leveraged loan carried a margin of about 6 percentage points above the benchmark. The potential bond yield is an all-in borrowing rate, while the older loan's quoted margin sits above its floating reference rate.

Ayala Chief Executive Cezar Consing said the Philippine conglomerate would receive about PHP20 billion from its Mitsubishi transaction and use proceeds to reduce debt, repurchase undervalued shares and fund growth. His comments supplied the intended cash allocation following the previously announced investment. The transaction remains expected to complete within Mitsubishi's fiscal year ending March 2027.

Deal activity continued to create prospective financing needs. JPMorgan's global M&A head Bouckaert said Wednesday that worldwide transactions totaling $2.5 trillion this year were likely to maintain momentum into 2027. Volume was about 35% above the same point last year, with technology transactions almost 60% higher. Royal Caribbean separately agreed to buy half of Sandals Resorts for about $3 billion. In private credit, however, Apollo was limiting redemptions from a fund for a third consecutive quarter amid investor concern over loan quality and legacy-software exposure.

After the U.S. fixed-income close, at 5:30 p.m. New York time, Royal Bank of Canada announced $1.5 billion of non-viability contingent capital subordinated debentures through its Canadian medium-term note program. They pay 4.67% until October 1, 2031, then quarterly interest at Daily Compounded CORRA plus 1.16 percentage points until October 1, 2036. Closing is expected October 1, 2026. Redemption at par from October 2031 requires prior OSFI approval and 30-60 days' notice; proceeds are for general business purposes.

## Capital Requirements and Recovery Prospects Change

UBS lost an important parliamentary vote over the form of capital it must hold against foreign subsidiaries. Switzerland's upper house voted 29-16 for equity backing of up to 90% of their value, only modestly below the government's original 100% proposal. UBS estimated the additional CET1 requirement at its domestic unit at about $16 billion; Goldman Sachs and Citigroup analysts put it near $17 billion.

The decision rejected the direction favored by UBS, which had sought substantially greater use of convertible AT1 debt. Existing AT1 securities rose as much as 0.3 cents to 98.36 cents after the vote as the prospect of extra issuance diminished. Under current rules, foreign units require 60% backing, a quarter of which can be met with AT1. The shift therefore matters both for equity retention and the future supply of subordinated instruments.

UBS said it would continue challenging the proposal. Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter argued that stronger equity backing would make overseas businesses easier to dispose of in a crisis and protect the Swiss parent. The bill now moves to the lower house, potentially for debate late this year; a final outcome is unlikely before 2027 and could involve a public vote. The AT1 market's favorable response came before those remaining legislative steps.

Thames Water's senior creditors were preparing larger concessions to avert special administration. London & Valley Water, whose members include Elliott, Silver Point and Farallon, was discussing a debt write-down of about 35%, up from the previously proposed 30%. The revised package could include roughly GBP3.5 billion of equity, compared with GBP3.35 billion proposed in March, and GBP6.55 billion of debt. Figures remained under negotiation, with a new proposal possible as early as October.

The creditors also proposed putting more than GBP1 billion into a dedicated performance-improvement fund, at least GBP200 million above their earlier provision. Thames faces up to GBP800 million of performance penalties by the end of the decade for failures including leaks and sewage spills; those sums would normally reduce customer bills. Creditors instead want the ring-fenced money used to repair operations, arguing that repeated penalties otherwise leave less cash to address the failures. Legal fines for environmental, drinking-water and other breaches would remain payable separately.

The proposed owners would take no dividends during a nine-year turnaround, with a eventual stock-market relisting envisaged if it succeeds. Their recovery alternative is material: a Teneo analysis prepared last year estimated that Class A creditors could receive as little as about 50 pence per pound under government control, depending on business performance. That estimate is a scenario, while the larger haircut and new funding remain proposed terms. Political opposition has already delayed the hoped-for regulatory agreement and consultation timetable.

At commodity trader Radiant World, new scrutiny focused on the assets available to support creditors. A September 8 balance sheet filed in court showed $1.007 billion of trade receivables within $1.072 billion of total assets, with the ten largest receivables accounting for 94%. Bloomberg's investigation found that much of the amount was attributed to counterparties disputing the debt, closely connected trading firms or difficult-to-locate entities.

The largest listed debtor, Glencore International, was shown owing $150.4 million, but Glencore had filed a notice offsetting amounts against sums owed to it and dismissed Radiant's related lawsuit as meritless. Vitol Asia was listed at $100.7 million; Vitol said it had stopped trading with Radiant months earlier and all transactions had been settled. Four apparently UAE-based companies accounted for $329 million, including $76 million attributed to Milla Sky Trading, whose registered representative said it had ceased trading a year earlier and denied knowledge of Radiant or the debt.

Radiant responded with screenshots of emails appearing to confirm debts from Milla Sky, Fly Horse and Bigbubble. Another $64.8 million receivable was attributed to Wuhan Iron & Steel Trading, which Bloomberg could not identify; people familiar with similarly named Wuhan Iron & Steel's parent, Baowu, said it recognized no such obligation. Radiant supplied an email confirmation for that amount as well. A further $298 million was assigned to closely connected companies, including Quanterra, Sapphire Minmetals and Grand Promise.

The dispute bears directly on the argument over control of the company. Founder Pinkesh Nahar says it is solvent and does not require judicial managers; Mizuho has alleged fraud and questioned the leadership's probity. Whether the receivables can be collected is central to the value available to creditors, with both the denials and Radiant's purported confirmations still part of the contested record.

Venezuela's debt process advanced diplomatically. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that Trump and interim President Delcy Rodriguez had discussed sovereign restructuring at Tuesday's UN reception, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also present. Rubio linked economic stabilization to rebuilding political parties, independent media and credible electoral institutions. The direct presidential discussion added U.S. political engagement to negotiations over about $60 billion of defaulted sovereign and PDVSA bonds, within much larger liabilities that include interest and arbitration claims.

European Union officials separately told Ukraine that further war funding required progress on legislation to reduce the shadow economy, strengthen tax revenues and align domestic rules with EU law. The condition places revenue reform alongside external financial support as part of Ukraine's funding challenge.

## Forward Market Significance

The September 24 Treasury buyback will test the reception of the expanded long-bond purchase program after Wednesday's announcement failed to steady prices. The consequential result is the amount and pricing of debt accepted against the $6 billion ceiling. Scheduled September 24 remarks from John Williams and Tom Barkin will address a policy debate now informed by much stronger national business surveys and Barr's assessment that inflation risks have risen as labor-market risks recede.

Japanese markets reopen September 24 after the Silver Week holiday to a changed U.S. rate backdrop and a yen that completed four consecutive daily declines. The reopening brings the overseas bond selloff into domestic trading after the BOJ's recent increase. Currency weakness could intensify imported-price concerns even as it helps exporters, while expectations of intervention remain a separate source of volatility.

Norway and Sweden announce policy decisions the same day, accompanied by new forecasts and rate paths. Wednesday's overnight swaps assigned a 60% probability to a Norwegian increase and 9% to a Swedish move. A quarter-point rise to 4.5% in Norway against an unchanged 1.75% in Sweden would widen their policy-rate gap to 275 basis points. Softer-than-expected Norwegian underlying inflation makes the first decision close; Sweden's forward guidance matters even if its rate remains unchanged, given stronger domestic momentum and external energy pressure.

After the U.S. close Wednesday, Bessent announced that Washington and Beijing had agreed to extend the Busan agreement through January 10 following his meeting with He Lifeng. That resolves the immediate question of an extension ahead of the September 24 Trump-Xi talks. Bessent said officials were examining whether a larger agreement could replace a succession of smaller ones. The leaders' meeting now tests the scope of that prospective arrangement, while the Iran negotiations face Pezeshkian's explicit conditions on sanctions and the blockade.

Corporate supply has its own near-term milestone: Citigroup will begin Paramount loan-investor meetings at 10:30 a.m. New York time on September 24, moving the previously announced acquisition financing toward distribution. The meetings follow completed AI financings that secured buyers but required high yields. Singapore's mid-October policy decision will meanwhile confront the newly reported acceleration in core prices, and Thames Water's revised proposal will test whether larger creditor losses and more operating funds can satisfy both regulators and the government.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off as stronger activity and a weak auction reinforce tightening expectations
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries fell sharply on September 23, with the 10-year yield rising 15 basis points to 5.11% over the session. Energy pressure gave way to a broader reassessment of growth and inflation after the U.S. composite PMI reached 58.4, its highest since July 2021, alongside faster input-cost inflation and longer supply delays. Fed Governor Michael Barr said further policy adjustments were likely needed as inflation risks increased and labor-market risks diminished.

The $70 billion 5-year auction accelerated the decline, clearing at 5.033% with a 3.1-basis-point tail and pushing the traded 5-year yield above 5% for the first time since 2007. Higher real yields accounted for most of the rise in the 10-year daily nominal reference, consistent with an expected policy response rather than an equally large increase in long-term inflation compensation. By the later session, swaps fully reflected three quarter-point increases over the following year.

U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly and high-yield spreads noticeably, yet corporate financing continued. SoftBank completed approximately $11 billion equivalent of dollar and euro borrowing at record issuance yields for its dollar bonds, while CoreWeave-linked developer Digital Drive priced $1.1 billion of notes at a 9.25% yield. The expanded $6 billion Treasury long-bond buyback announced for September 24 failed to steady prices ahead of the operation.
